layman_headline: Market cooling off after a massive rally week — no new entries warranted right now.
layman_explanation: Bitcoin just surged 22% in a week and is now taking a breather below $80,000. Almost everything in the top 20 is pulling back after huge gains. Our existing XRP position is down about 10% from entry — it ran up 40% this week but we bought near the top of that move. The swing candidates available right now are either already overbought, are stablecoins, or are low-liquidity tokens with poor risk profiles.
layman_action: Hold tight and be patient. Our XRP position hasn't hit its stop-loss at $1.30, so we let it ride. Don't chase any of these extended moves — wait for a proper pullback to create a safer entry on a quality asset.
expert_reasoning: The entire market just experienced a massive 7-day rally (BTC +22%, ETH +28.5%, XRP +40.5%, ZEC +55%) and is now in a natural consolidation/pullback phase. All swing candidates with meaningful moves are extended — PUMP has an RSI of 86, LIT is up 47%, MON up 28%. BTW is the only mean-reversion candidate but has dropped 41% in a week with no technical data, no RSI, no volume comparison — it's a knife-catch with undefined risk. BTC dominance at 59.2% continues to pressure alts. Fear & Greed dropping from 74 to 65 suggests the euphoria is fading. CryptoSlate notes BTC's rally is flipping from short squeeze to long squeeze, which is a bearish signal. The prudent move is to hold XRP (still above stop-loss) and wait for better setups.
risk_factors: XRP could break below $1.30 stop-loss if the broader market correction deepens from this overbought state
BTC failing to reclaim $80K could trigger a larger pullback that drags all alts down significantly
Three critical US economic reports arriving could inject unexpected volatility
watch_list: BTC price action around $78K-$80K — a decisive break above $80K would re-energize alts, a breakdown below $76K would be bearish
XRP price relative to $1.30 stop-loss — if it breaks, we exit immediately
US economic data releases and their impact on risk assets — could set the tone for the next few days
market_context: The crypto market is in a natural consolidation after an explosive 7-day rally. BTC dominance remains elevated at 59.2%, and Fear & Greed has cooled from 74 to 65, suggesting momentum is fading and this is not the time to chase.
context_banner: Post-rally consolidation underway — patience is the best trade until pullbacks create defined-risk entries.

key_signals.description: Bitcoin's rally is flipping from short squeeze to long squeeze, suggesting upside momentum may be exhausting and a deeper pullback is possible.
Fear & Greed dropped from 74 to 65 in one day — euphoria is cooling, which often precedes further consolidation or correction after big rallies.
PUMP's RSI at 86 is deeply overbought — the only candidate with RSI data confirms the broader market is extended and poor for new entries.
Bitcoin ETFs absorbed $2.5B in 7 days but supply absorption is now the 'key question' as BTC fails to reclaim $80K, signaling potential resistance.
No volume breakout signals present in any swing candidate — lack of volume confirmation makes chasing extended moves especially risky.
